newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel urges more pressure on Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel urges more pressure on Hun Sen.

text.p: A U.S. House of Representatives panel called on Thursday for stepped-up international action to resolve the crisis in Cambodia sparked by the ousting of First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh this month.

The subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific urged the Clinton administration to seek an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council to "consider all options to restore peace" in Cambodia.

Ranariddh was removed from his share of power in a bloody coup on July 5 by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen. U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, on her way to meet her regional counterparts in Kuala Lumpur, vowed on Wednesday to keep pressure on Hun Sen to accept mediation and restore a true coalition government.

In a unanimously adopted resolution, the House panel said the United States should seek an emergency meeting of donor countries to press for an aid suspension "to encourage respect for democratic processes, constitutionalism and the rule of law" in Cambodia.

The Sense of the House resolution, which would not have the force of law, calls for a continued suspension of U.S. aid until violence ends, a democratically elected government is reconstituted and steps are taken to ensure free and fair elections in 1998.
The measure, which goes next to the full House International Relations Committee, also calls for holding up U.S. aid until the military is depoliticized and the judiciary is made independent.

The Clinton administration announced a 30-day suspension of aid to Cambodia after the coup to underline U.S. disapproval of Hun Sen's power play. The administration has said it is reviewing military and economic aid programmes to determine which should be suspended indefinitely.
